metaDescription: Five iPad stands compared on size range, stability, height and portability, from compact desk docks to a 65 inch floor tripod for hands-free viewing.
introParagraphs: An iPad stand sounds simple until you consider how differently people use one. Some want a small desk dock for video calls, some want a tall floor stand beside a recliner, and some need to carry it in a bag. The five picks here cover that range, from the UGREEN at about 4.7 by 4.2 inches folded to the SAMHOUSING tripod that extends from 16.7 to 65 inches.

Size support is the first spec to check. The UGREEN accepts devices from 4 to 11 inches, the Lamicall 4 to 13 inches, and the tounee 4.7 to 16.9 inches. The LISEN weighs 15.2 ounces and uses a gravity-based hold, while the tounee adds a locking mechanism and an all-metal alloy base.

We evaluated each stand using product specs and buyer feedback, focusing on how stable it stays, how easily it adjusts, and how well it fits an iPad in a case. This guide is written for active adults and the family members buying for them, so the advice favors simple adjustment and a stable base over gimmicks.

products.name: Lamicall Adjustable iPad Stand
products.description:
The Lamicall Adjustable iPad Stand is a sturdy aluminum dock that fits devices from 4 to 13 inches, covering every iPad from mini to Pro. It adjusts for vertical and horizontal viewing. Rubber pads and feet protect the device and keep the stand from sliding on a desk.

The hook width is 18 millimeters, so check that your iPad and case fit that gap. It is a balanced choice that does most things well without specializing. It suits people who want one dependable desk stand without a complicated setup.

Setup takes seconds, and the metal body wipes clean. It is not the tallest stand here, so it works best at a desk rather than for reading from a recliner. Compared with the UGREEN it supports up to 13 inches instead of 11, and compared with the tounee it is simpler but less adjustable in height.
products.bestFor: Most iPad owners who want a sturdy desk dock
cons: 18 mm hook width limits thick cases
Not height adjustable like the tounee

products.name: tounee Dual Rod Aluminum Stand

specList.label: Design
specList.value: Dual rod, locking height and angle

products.description:
The tounee Dual Rod Aluminum Stand uses a locking mechanism to set height and angle, and it supports devices from 4.7 to 16.9 inches. The sturdy all-metal alloy base keeps it stable. It also works with Surface tablets, so households with mixed devices can share it.

The dual rod design gives more height control than a simple hook dock, but it also means more parts to adjust. It suits people with large iPads who want to raise the screen toward eye level. The locking mechanism is worth testing on arrival to ensure it holds under tapping.

Aluminum wipes clean, and the metal base adds heft. It is not pocket-size, so it lives on a desk. Compared with the Lamicall, it supports larger screens and adjusts height, while the UGREEN is far more portable.
pros: Works with Surface and other tablets
cons: More adjustment steps than a simple dock

products.name: UGREEN Foldable iPad Stand
products.description:
The UGREEN Tablet Stand is the compact choice, folding to roughly 4.7 by 4.2 inches. It holds 4 to 11 inch devices at angles from 15 to 100 degrees. That covers iPad mini, iPad Air and 11 inch iPad Pro.

Its limits are clear: the maximum device thickness is 0.55 inches including the case, and screens above 11 inches do not fit. A bulky protective case may push the iPad past the limit. It suits slim-cased iPads and anyone who wants a stand that disappears into a drawer.

It needs no assembly, and the foldable design fits in a pocket or bag. Compared with the Lamicall, it is smaller and cheaper in spirit but fits fewer sizes, and compared with the LISEN it gives a tighter grip.
pros: Fits iPad mini through 11 inch Pro
cons: Case plus iPad must stay under 0.55 inches

products.name: LISEN Foldable iPad Stand

specList.label: Adjustment
specList.value: Height and angle with truss rod

products.description:
The LISEN iPad Stand folds flat and weighs 15.2 ounces, or 0.95 pounds. It uses a gravity-based system, with no clips or magnets, relying on back tilt to hold the iPad. A bridge screw truss rod keeps it extended and steady.

There is nothing to clamp, so you can drop the iPad in and out quickly. The tradeoff is that you must set the back tilt correctly and use it on a firm surface. It suits people who swap between iPad and other devices and dislike grips.

At nearly a pound it is not the lightest, but it is built to stand firm. It folds flat for travel. Compared with the UGREEN, it is heavier and more structural, and compared with the Lamicall it relies on gravity instead of a hook grip.
cons: Needs correct back tilt on a firm surface
At 0.95 lb it is heavier than dock stands

products.name: SAMHOUSING iPad Tripod Floor Stand
products.description:
The SAMHOUSING iPad Tripod Stand is a floor stand with four height settings from 16.7 to 65 inches. The holder rotates 360 degrees, and a remote is included. It lets you place an iPad beside a chair, bed or treadmill without a table.

It is the most specialized pick here. The tripod needs floor space and a stable surface, and it is not designed to move between rooms daily. It suits people who watch or video chat from a recliner or bed and want a hands-free setup.

Setup involves extending the legs and choosing a height level. The tripod stores upright in a corner. Compared with the Lamicall, it adds height and distance, while the UGREEN is the opposite: low and portable.
products.bestFor: Recliner or bedside viewing without a table
cons: Takes floor space and is not portable
Tripod legs can be a trip hazard

buyingCriteria.explanation: Ranges differ widely: the UGREEN supports 4 to 11 inches, the Lamicall 4 to 13 inches, and the tounee 4.7 to 16.9 inches. Typical stands top out near 13 inches, so a 12.9 inch iPad Pro is the usual borderline case. Measure your iPad with its case. If you may upgrade later, buy for the larger size.

The UGREEN allows 0.55 inches including the case and the Lamicall uses an 18 millimeter hook width. Rugged cases quickly exceed those numbers. Measure the thickest part of your iPad with the case on and compare to the spec. A gravity-based design like the LISEN avoids the hook width problem.

The tounee has an all-metal alloy base and the SAMHOUSING tripod relies on its leg spread. Research shows taller arms behave like levers and need a heavier base, with some guides placing 4.5 pounds as a minimum for a full-size iPad at full extension. A light dock like the UGREEN is fine near the table. For tall setups, choose the heavier base.

The SAMHOUSING reaches 65 inches and the tounee adjusts height with a locking mechanism, while the Lamicall and UGREEN sit low. Raising the screen toward eye level reduces forward neck bend. Video calls also look better when the camera sits near eye level. Use a tall stand for long sessions and a low dock for short ones.

The UGREEN covers 15 to 100 degrees, the LISEN uses a bridge screw rod, and the tounee uses a locking mechanism. Hardly any listings document one-handed adjustment, yet it matters for stiff hands. Look for joints that hold their position without drooping. Test the stand for a few days and return it if it slips.

The UGREEN folds to about 4.7 by 4.2 inches and the LISEN folds flat, while the tounee and SAMHOUSING are more permanent. If the stand moves between rooms, weight and fold size matter most. A stand that stays in one place can be larger and more stable. Be honest about how often you will carry it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared base materials and structures, from the tounee all-metal alloy base to the SAMHOUSING tripod legs. The more stable picks scored higher. We based this on specs and buyer feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and case compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked each stand's range, from the UGREEN at 4 to 11 inches to the tounee at 16.9 inches. We also noted case limits such as 0.55 inches. The Lamicall offered the best balance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at angle and height control, from the SAMHOUSING at four height levels to the UGREEN's 15 to 100 degrees. Simple, secure locks scored best. The most basic fixed-feeling option is the LISEN's gravity hold.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We rewarded stands that fold small, like the UGREEN. The tripod and tounee are the least portable. Weight in a bag mattered.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use for older users
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered grips that are easy to operate and that hold without fiddling. Gravity holds and simple hooks ranked well. Multi-step locks counted slightly against.

cards.label: Desk dock
cards.text: The Lamicall, UGREEN, LISEN and tounee sit on a table. They are compact and quick to use. They need a flat surface.

cards.label: Floor stand
cards.text: The SAMHOUSING stands from 16.7 to 65 inches beside a chair or bed. It needs floor space. It is best for hands-free viewing.

howToChoose.note: Choose the Lamicall for a desk and the SAMHOUSING for a recliner.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A camera at roughly eye level, a stable base, and angle control. Low tablets show chins and ceilings.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The tounee raises a large iPad with its locking height, and the SAMHOUSING reaches 65 inches for standing calls. The Lamicall suits a normal desk setup.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a 12.9 inch iPad Pro or need height. The tounee supports up to 16.9 inches and the SAMHOUSING reaches 65 inches.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a smaller iPad and a flat desk. The LISEN is the lowest-cost pick and the UGREEN adds portability.

faq.q: How do I choose between a dock stand and a tripod floor stand?
faq.a: A dock such as the Lamicall sits on a table and keeps the iPad close, while the SAMHOUSING tripod stands from 16.7 to 65 inches beside a chair or bed. Choose a dock for desk work and a tripod for hands-free viewing away from a table. Many households end up using one of each.

faq.q: How much should an iPad stand cost?
faq.a: Prices range from the lowest-cost LISEN to the premium tounee. You mostly pay for size range and metal construction. A mid-range dock handles most needs.
Check the numbers. The UGREEN allows 0.55 inches including the case and the Lamicall uses an 18 millimeter hook width. A gravity stand such as the LISEN avoids hook limits.
They can if the base is light. Research notes that a high arm acts as a lever and needs a heavier base for a full-size iPad. The tounee uses an all-metal alloy base to address this.

faq.q: Can one stand work with other tablets?
faq.a: Yes. The tounee lists support for iPads and Surface tablets, and the Lamicall covers 4 to 13 inch tablets and phones. Always check the screen range.

faq.q: How do I clean an aluminum stand?
faq.a: Wipe it with a soft damp cloth and dry it. Avoid harsh cleaners near rubber pads. Check hinges and rods for grit.
